bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen denies Blackwell delays; Mitsubishi Heavy partnership for AI datacenters
bullets.body: Jensen Huang publicly debunked rumors of delays on 800V and rack-to-rack optical interconnects, stating both remain on original timeline. Separately, Nikkei reports Mitsubishi Heavy partnering with NVIDIA on AI datacenter cooling and energy management systems for next-gen plants. NVIDIA also promoting its Vera Rubin NVL72 compute tray delivering 200 AI petaFLOPs.

bullets.title: NVDA: China H200 approval denied; Asia buyer list halved amid chip crackdown
bullets.body: FT reports Chinese tech firms are lobbying Beijing to approve Nvidia H200 sales but approval has not been granted and large-scale sales remain unlikely. Separately, NVIDIA is halving its Asia buyer list as part of the China chip export crackdown, signaling a meaningful reduction in addressable market in the region.

bullets.title: MU: IBD Top 50 #1 rank; bullish consolidation with $1,100–$1,200 price targets
bullets.body: Micron is ranked #1 on the IBD Top 50 list, described as forming a multi-week consolidation along its 50-day moving average with an expected breakout this week to $1,100–$1,200. Separately, MU announced an additional $3B investment in U.S. semiconductor supply chain focused on HBM for AI, and large bullish options flow was flagged on the tape.

bullets.title: Photonics sector narrative shift: CPO delayed, copper lasting longer, NPO emerging
bullets.body: Fintwit photonics commentary clusters around a key narrative update: Scale Up CPO adoption is further away than previously anticipated, copper interconnects are outperforming expectations, and NPO plus 'Scale Across' are emerging as the next dominant themes. Substrate layer production uptick seen as positive for AXTI, COHR, LITE, AAOI supply chain. Morgan Stanley CPO note identifies COHR, LITE for lasers; TSEM for silicon photonics; MRVL/Celestial and POET for optical engines.

bullets.title: LITE: $919M Texas AI-server BBU plant investment signals capex acceleration
bullets.body: Taiwan's Lite-On Technology announced a $919M investment in a McKinney, Texas manufacturing facility focused on Battery Backup Units for AI servers, adding to its existing Plano, Texas plant. 2026 capex expected to rise from NT$13B.

bullets.title: META: Analyst reversal to bullish on open-source strategy; social graph as AI moat
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst reversed a prior bearish META call, crediting the open-source/Llama pivot as the right strategic move and praising execution over the past 9–12 months. A second analyst highlighted META's social graph and ecosystem density as a structural advantage for building personal AI agents and developer platforms. META also noted closing above its 200-day MA for two consecutive days, longest such streak since February.

bullets.title: Samsung Foundry secures Anthropic as customer; explores U.S. ADR listing
bullets.body: Korean local media reports Samsung's foundry division has agreed to manufacture Anthropic's custom AI chips, following recent wins with Tesla and NVIDIA. Separately, Samsung is in preliminary discussions with banks about a potential U.S. ADR share offering, though no final decision has been made.

bullets.title: UMC achieves first mass-produced silicon photonics from Singapore; Citi positive
bullets.body: UMC announced the first mass-produced silicon photonics wafers from its Singapore facility. SILITH and UMC are reported to have achieved a mass production milestone for silicon photonics, with Citi seeing an improving outlook.

bullets.title: Lightmatter joins NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem for CPO/NPO optical interconnect
bullets.body: Lightmatter has joined NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion ecosystem, adapting its bidirectional optical-link architecture to NVLink specs to supply CPO and NPO products. The goal is to reduce fiber and connector counts while maintaining compatibility with NVIDIA's SerDes technologies. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged this as 'real signal, not hype.'

bullets.title: HBM demand as the key variable for duration of memory boom
bullets.body: Analyst commentary coalesces around the view that HBM demand will determine how long the memory sector boom lasts—if HBM demand declines, the memory cycle ends. Separately, Innolight investor relations takeaways note 1.6T market demand has not contracted and 800G demand was revised meaningfully higher vs prior expectations.

bullets.title: AAOI: CPO laser design wins lacking; CPO timeline 'TBD' per CEO
bullets.body: Analysis notes AAOI derives revenue primarily from pluggable optical modules and is still in the reliability-work phase for CPO-related lasers, with no design wins and a 'TBD' commercial timing per the CEO. MTSI appears to have lost momentum in the CPO laser competition.

bullets.title: NBIS: 40% prepayment on MSFT and META contracts improves IRR math
bullets.body: Fintwit pushback on a bearish NBIS thesis: NBIS received a 40% prepayment on its Microsoft contract and likely a similar prepayment on its Meta contract, which materially improves capital employed and project IRR—a point critics say the bear case omits.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hits new all-time highs; Siri AI seen as Apple Watch catalyst; M7 Ultra roadmap
bullets.body: Apple hit new all-time highs during the session. Separately, reviewers note Siri AI upgrades make Apple Watch 'finally feel like a wrist computer.' Apple's M7 Ultra chip (expected 2029) is rumored to support 1.5TB of RAM. A competitor (OnePlus) is reportedly exiting the U.S. market, seen as creating more profitable room for Apple.

bullets.title: Fed: 45% July hike probability; CPI and Warsh testimony are the key catalysts
bullets.body: Detailed thread from a credible macro account lays out the framework: Fed funds futures price 45% probability of a July 29 hike. A 0.3% core CPI print implies July hike; 0.2% creates July vs. September debate (September 104% priced); 0.1% implies September. Headline CPI expected at -0.1% due to gasoline (-0.4%). Waller's hawkish speech also repriced hike odds higher on Polymarket and SOFR futures. Warsh House testimony at 9 AM Tuesday is the other key catalyst.

bullets.title: Oil surges ~10% on U.S.-Iran escalation; Strait of Hormuz disruption risk elevated
bullets.body: WTI settled at $78.14/bbl (+9.42%) and Brent at $83.30/bbl (+9.59%), the largest single-day oil moves since 2020. Trump announced Iran strikes and proposed a 20% fee on Strait of Hormuz cargo (~$30M per loaded supertanker). Polymarket puts Hormuz normalization before 2027 at very low odds. Iran threatened to fire on any vessel transiting the strait without warning.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield hits 4.63%, 30-year at 5.1%; real yields near 2024 highs
bullets.body: Treasury yields surged with 10-year at 4.63% and 30-year at 5.1%, driven by rising oil prices stoking inflation concerns and Waller's hawkish Fed speech. 2-year yields hit highest since February 2025. Real yields (not breakevens) drove the move, nearing 2024 peaks.

bullets.title: China June trade data blows out estimates: exports +27% YoY, imports +36% YoY
bullets.body: China's June trade balance surged to $125.62B (est. $120.10B, prior $105.43B). Exports rose 27% YoY vs. 19% estimate, driven by AI hardware demand and tariff front-loading. Imports jumped 36% YoY vs. 26.1% estimate. Customs Vice Minister noted strong AI-related product export growth in H1.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler debt spreads hit 150bps record high; $700B debt accumulation flagged
bullets.body: Hyperscaler basket credit spreads crossed 150bps for the first time ever. Fintwit commentary highlights that Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle have collectively accumulated nearly $700B in debt tied to AI datacenter capex. One account adds that hyperscaler creditors are concerned they're financing loans against rapidly depreciating memory chips.

bullets.title: INTC: €5B European manufacturing expansion announced
bullets.body: Intel Foundry announced a €5B investment to expand advanced semiconductor manufacturing in Europe, including upgrades to its Ireland facility.

bullets.title: HOOD: Robinhood Chain hits 750K accounts; exploring $400M+ asset-backed securities offering
bullets.body: Robinhood Chain cumulative daily accounts exceeded 750,000. Separately, HOOD is reportedly gauging investor interest in at least $400M in asset-backed securities backed by its branded consumer credit card receivables—its first such offering.
